1.	INTRODUCTION 2. COMPONENTS 3. COMPONENT SETUP 2.1. GENERAL COMPONENTS 2.2. PLAYER COMPONENTS 2.3. SOLO MODE COMPONENTS 3.1. THE WALK OF THE APOSTLES From the heart of Prague’s Old Town, the ancient Astronomical Clock, known as Orloj, marks the passage of time with its intricate mechanism and enigmatic figures: a marvel of medieval technology that still endures to this day. The astronomical dial, the oldest part of the clock, dates back to 1410, but the game is set around 1865, when the calendar, painted by Josef Mánes, and the apostle moving figures were added to the clock. From their workshop, each player will construct the signs of the zodiac and the calendar months, as well as the images of the apostles. With each construction, you will be one step closer to completing this masterpiece, a symbol of the city of Prague. 1 Main board 1 Rotation axis 1 Orloj clock face 1 Astronomical dial 1 Moon disc 1 Walk of the apostles 3 Orloj crowning pieces 2 Apostle gears 3 Plastic rotation axes (1 spare) 1 Golden rooster 1 Round marker 1 Painter 12 Calendar sections 12 Month dials 6 Blocked month dials 12 Zodiac dials 6 Blocked zodiac dials 1 Large final construction dial 2 Hammer discs 18 Assistants (3 of each type) 24 Scrolls (red seal) 6 Royal scrolls (blue seal) 6 Mastery stained-glass windows 9 Common stained-glasswindow objectives (3 of each colour) 9 Common objective bonuses (3 of each colour) 21 Workshop cards 6 Hammer cards 8 Initial resource cards 4 Additional actions reference cards 15 Gold pieces 20 Paint pieces 20 Wood pieces 20 Iron pieces 18 Coins 1 Bag 1 Personal board 1 Forge 1 Warehouse 18 Action cards 3 Basic turn scoring cards 3 Production cubes 1 Hammer cube 1 Rooster disc 14 Workers 1 Sculptor 3 Mastery discs 1 Scoring marker 1 Personal set of 12 apostle tiles numbered from 1 to 12 with their backs in the player’s colour 5 Deviation tokens 3 Advanced turn scoring cards 1 Endgame scoring card 5 Scoring tiles 3 Mastery tiles 3 Mastery track tiles 3 End-of-round action tiles 1 Conditions met tile 1 mastery track objective tile Assemble the gears onto the walk of the apostles. To do this, fit the gears together so that in the lower position, Apostle 1 (James) is displayed on the left side and Apostle 2 (Peter) on the right side. This will be the initial position for each game. Use the plastic axes included in the game for assembly.

4. GAME SETUP 4.1. GENERAL SETUP Randomly take one of the Orloj crowning pieces and assemble it with the walk of the apostles. Place the round marker on the leftmost space of the round track according to the number of players in the game. Then, place the golden rooster on the general rooster track on the number indicated by the marker on the round track. Note: One of the crowning pieces is only for solo mode. For the first game: Take the crowning piece marked with the symbol . Shuffle the 6 mastery stained-glass windows and randomly place 3 of them at the top of the mastery tracks. Return the rest to the box. Take the 6 royal scrolls (blue seal), shuffle them and place 3 of them face up at the top of the mastery tracks. Return the rest to the box. Take the scrolls (red seal) according to the number of players. In a four-player game, use all the scrolls. Remove from the game the scrolls marked with a in a three-player game, and in a two-player or solo mode game, also remove those marked with a . Return the unused scrolls to the box. Shuffle the scrolls to form a face-down reserve next to the main board, then reveal three or four of them, depending on whether it is a game with 1-2 players or a game with more than 2 players, respectively. Take the common stained-glass-window objectives and separate them by the colour of their backs. Shuffle each colour separately and place one of each colour in the corresponding positions according to their backs. Return the rest to the box. Draw, at random, the number of dials indicated in the table on the left based on the number of players. In the construction area, place a blocked month dial in each space indicated by the dials drawn from the bag. Draw 1 more dial from the bag and place all extracted dials, each in its corresponding space in the calendar with their illustrated side up. Place all remaining dials still in the bag in the construction area in their corresponding spaces, but with the nonillustrated side up. The image shows the setup for a four-player game. To set up the calendar, take the month dials, place them in the bag and follow these steps: Place a hammer disc in the indicated position in each of the construction zones (months and zodiac). Take the 12 calendar sections, shuffle them and place them face up in a random order to form a circle around the calendar. Take the main board and unfold it in the centre of the table. Place the Orloj clock face and the astronomical dial on the rotation axis in the centre to form the clock, as shown in the image. Take the moon disc and place it in the first position to the left of the hand inside the astronomical dial. As the starting position for each game, the Orloj clock face should be placed in a random position and the astronomical dial with the hand pointing to the starting hour of the game. E.g. The image shows the setup for a game starting between 1:00 p.m. and 1:59 p.m. Place the walk of the apostles with its gears above the main board. Rotate the gears until apostles 1 and 2 (James and Peter) are visible at the bottom. E.g. The image shows the placement of the round marker and the rooster for a two-player game. Prepare the zodiac dials in the same way as the month dials. Place the large final construction dial in the centre of the calendar with the side shown in the image facing up. Take the common objective bonuses and separate them by the colour of their backs. Shuffle each colour separately and place one of each colour in the corresponding positions according to their backs. Return the rest to the box. Shuffle the 21 workshop cards and place 3 of them in the designated spaces on the main board. Place the rest of the deck aside. For the first game: Store the 12 sections in the box and use the setup printed on the board. Place the painter in the position indicated in the image. Take the assistants and place them next to the board in 6 separate piles. Each pile should contain assistants of the same type (with the same iconography). Additionally, each pile should have 1 assistant less than the number of players in the game. Return any remaining assistants to the box. In solo mode, as well as in a two-player game, there will be only 1 assistant of each type. Take the resources (gold, paint, wood, iron and coins) and place them next to the main board to form a general supply.

4.2. INDIVIDUAL PLAYER SETUP 5. GENERAL CONCEPTS 4.3. HAMMERS AND INITIAL RESOURCES 5.1. IMMEDIATE AND ENDGAME VICTORY POINTS 5.3. DEVIATION TOKENS 5.4. WORKERS Each player performs these steps: Place your personal board in the centre of your play area, along with your warehouse and forge. Place your 5 deviation tokens at the top of your personal board so the side that does not show the gear icon is facing up. Place your rooster disc in the first position of your personal rooster track, starting from the bottom. Place one cube in the bottom position of each production track and your forge track. Place your workers in the indicated positions: Three in the apostle panel Three in the production zone One above each workshop card on the main board. Place the rest of your workers next to your personal board. These are your available workers. In three- and four-player games, return one of these workers to the box. In three- and four-player games, each player has four available workers. Place your sculptor next to your personal board. Place one mastery disc on the lowest space of each mastery track on the main board. Each player places their hammer card underneath their forge and takes the resources indicated on the initial resource card. If this card also includes apostles, take them from your personal set and place them in your warehouse. You may wait to take the resources from your initial resource card until just before your first turn to know the position of the astronomical dial and the Orloj clock face. Place your scoring marker on space 10 of the scoring track on the main board. Take your personal set of apostle tiles (with the back in your colour and numbered from 1 to 12) and place them next to your personal board. Deal each player an additional actions reference card. The last player to have visited the city of Prague will be the starting player. Shuffle the hammer cards and reveal one more than the number of players. Then, place one initial resource card next to each of these hammer cards to form combinations. Starting with the last player and proceeding counterclockwise, each player chooses one of these combinations. The image shows the hammer setup for a two-player game. For the first game: instead of assembling combinations randomly, use the four preset initial setups, following the number in the lower right corner of each card. Randomly distribute one of these combinations to each player. In the game, there are two types of scoring: immediate scoring and endgame scoring. From now on, we will refer to Victory Points as VP. This icon indicates that this scoring is resolved immediately. Move your marker forward on the scoring track as many spaces as the icon indicates. This icon indicates that this scoring is resolved at the end of the game. Do not move your marker yet. In Orloj, there are different types of resources. A resource icon indicates that you take a resource from the general supply and place it in your play area. Conversely, whenever you see a resource icon crossed out with an , it indicates a cost that you must pay by returning the indicated resource to the general supply. 5.2. RESOURCES 5.2.1. Basic resources 5.4.1. Recovering workers 5.4.2. Unlocking new workers 5.2.2. Special resources Take one gold from the general supply and place it in your personal reserve. Pay one gold. Return it to the general supply. Paint, wood and iron are the basic resources in the game. This icon is equivalent to one basic resource of your choice: paint, wood, or iron. Due to the gold elements of Orloj, gold is an essential resource for construction in the game. On the other hand, coins represent money and are related to the mastery tracks. The Univerzita Karlova in Prague is one of the oldest universities in Europe and access to it was reserved for the wealthiest classes. Gold and coins are special resources in Orloj. You can pay a special resource instead of any basic resource. However, you cannot pay with coins instead of gold or vice versa. You can also obtain gold through basic resources. You can exchange three identical basic resources for one gold. You may perform this exchange at any time during your turn. Clock construction is a delicate process, but sometimes you must force the mechanism and later correct it. By forcing deviation, you will be able to perform additional movements beyond the permitted limits in the game’s moving parts or fulfill conditions required for certain actions. However, be careful—these tokens may also cause you to lose points during the rooster’s call. Forcing deviation: This icon indicates that you must flip one of your deviation tokens, revealing the broken gear icon. Correcting deviation: This icon indicates that you may flip a deviation token back, hiding the broken gear icon. Each player has 5 deviation tokens available on their board. You cannot force a deviation if all your tokens already show the broken gear icon. Whenever a force deviation icon appears next to an action, you must first force the deviation before performing the action. One of the key mechanics in Orloj is worker management. If, at any point in the game, you do not have available workers, you will be forced to pass your turn or find alternative ways to unlock or recover new workers. When you recover workers, you may take those that were used on the clock or the calendar, making them available again. Note: Normally, workers are recovered only from the clock. Recovering them from the calendar may result in earning fewer VP at the end of the game. Recover one worker. Recover two workers. Recover the indicated number of workers. At the beginning of the game, you start with a set number of available workers. However, during the game, you will be able to unlock new workers and place them next to your personal board as available workers. The methods for unlocking workers are explained in their respective sections: ● Unlocking workers from your apostle panel. See section 10.1. Placing an apostle on page 14. ● Unlocking workers from workshop cards. See section 8.7. Expanding the workshop on page 12. ● Unlocking workers in your production zone. See section 8.6. Performing an upgrade on page 11.

5.5. MASTERY TRACKS 5.7. WAREHOUSE 7.1. ACTIVATING THE CLOCK MECHANISM 7.2. PASSING 8.1. RESOURCE PRODUCTION 5.6. CLOCK MECHANISM 6. GAME FLOW 7. THE TURN 8. ACTIONS There are three mastery tracks in the game: Innovation, Precision and Observation. Each of these tracks corresponds to a skill that improves based on the position of your mastery disc. The training and knowledge of a clockmaker are their greatest virtues! Innovation Track (blue): Indicates the maximum rotation of the astronomical dial allowed without forcing deviation. See section 5.6. Clock Mechanism on page 8. Precision Track (pink): Indicates the steps to take when a player passes their turn. See section 7.2. Passing on page 9. Also determines the sculptor’s level. See section 8.9. Activating the Sculptor on page 13. Outer Ring: Printed on the main board, divided into sections. Orloj clock face: Always moves counterclockwise and is divided into sections. Astronomical dial: Always moves clockwise. The hand of the astronomical dial indicates the actions a player performs on their turn. Moon: The moon moves clockwise along the astronomical dial and serves as the most efficient way to correct deviations. The warehouse is where apostles and assistants go. There are two available spaces in your warehouse—one space is exclusively for storing an apostle, while the other can hold either an apostle or an assistant. You may rearrange the apostles and assistants in your warehouse at any time. The game begins with the starting player’s turn. From then on, players take their turns in a clockwise order until the game ends. On each turn, you have two options: Activate the clock mechanism Pass Regardless of the chosen option and at any point during your turn, you may perform any number of additional actions. See section 10. Additional turn actions on page 14. You must have at least one available worker to choose this option. Configure the clock so that the hand of the astronomical dial points to a section of the outer ring and a section of the Orloj clock face. To do this, follow these steps: Configure the astronomical dial. The astronomical dial always rotates clockwise and must move at least one space. The maximum movement capacity of the astronomical dial is indicated by the height of your disc on the blue mastery track. You may force deviation to rotate additional spaces. Force as many deviations as the extra spaces you wish to move the astronomical dial. Configure the Orloj clock face. The Orloj clock face always rotates counterclockwise and you are not required to move it. Force as many deviations as the number of spaces you wish to rotate the dial. Note: The astronomical dial and the Orloj clock face are two independent components and rotating one does not affect the other. Place one of your available workers on the space indicated by the hand. If there is already a worker in that space, return it to the player it belongs to. You may return your own worker to yourself. Choose whether to perform the actions of the outer ring section first or the Orloj clock face section first. You cannot alternate actions between each section. Mikel wants to perform the build action, but since he is only allowed one rotation on the blue mastery track , he must force two deviations to move three spaces to the desired position . In addition to these two, he decides to force one more deviation to rotate the Orloj clock face . He returns the worker to Carlos, places his own and chooses whether to resolve the outer ring section first or the Orloj clock face section first . Instead of activating the clock mechanism, you may pass. Typically, the pass action is done to recover workers, but you may also choose to pass even if you still have available workers in your play area. The pass action is linked to the height of your disc on the pink mastery track and is divided into three steps: Recover as many workers as indicated by the height of your mastery disc on the pink mastery track. See section 5.4.1. Recovering workers on page 7. Activate the moon. See section 8.4. Activating the moon on page 11. Move the golden rooster one space to the right on the general rooster track. Below are the game’s actions. These actions are not mandatory and if a player does not wish to or cannot perform an action during their turn, they simply skip it. Produce as many resources as indicated by your production track. Eduardo performs the iron production action. Since his production cube is at the highest level, he produces two iron and one gold. This icon indicates that you take one resource of your choice out of wood, paint or iron. This icon indicates that you produce resources from a production track of your choice.

8.2. MASTERY 8.3. TAKING AN APOSTLE 8.4. ACTIVATING THE MOON 8.5. MOVING THE PAINTER 8.6. PERFORMING AN UPGRADE 8.2.1. Bonuses on the mastery tracks Move one of your discs up one space on the mastery track indicated by the icon colour. Move one of your discs up one space on a mastery track of your choice. Pay one coin and move one of your discs up one space on a mastery track of your choice. Gain one point if, upon receiving a mastery, you were already on the last space of the track. Within the mastery tracks, there are different rewards that are obtained when your mastery disc reaches the indicated position for the bonus. Scrolls (red seal): Take one scroll from those revealed on the main board, then replace it with a new one from the pile. Scrolls can be used as additional actions in a turn. See section 10.3. Using a scroll on page 15. Keep this scroll in your play area, whether you have used it or not. Royal Scrolls (blue seal): Score immediately, based on the condition indicated on the scroll, up to a maximum of 10 VP. Keep this scroll in your play area after scoring it. No other player can score a royal scroll that has already been scored. All royal scrolls are described in section 13 of the Appendix: Royal scrolls on page 22. Moon: Gain one moon activation action. See section 8.4. Activating the moon on page 11. Assistant: Take an assistant from one of the stacks and place it in the designated space in your warehouse. Assistants can be used as additional actions during the turn. See section 10.4. Placing an assistant on page 15. You cannot have two identical assistants with the same iconography. Sculptor Level: This indicator shows your sculptor’s level when performing an action with them. See section 8.9. Activating the sculptor on page 13. To give it an authentic touch, we work on the walk of the apostles, a spectacle in which, every hour, the rooster crows and the apostles appear over the Orloj in a synchronized choreography. Take one of the two apostles displayed at the bottom of the gears from your personal set and place it in your warehouse. Then, rotate the gears to the next position to reveal a new combination of apostles. The rotation direction of the gears is indicated at their centre. You cannot take an apostle if your warehouse is full. Before taking an apostle, you may choose to rotate the gears. Force as many deviation tokens as spaces you wish to rotate the gears before taking the apostle. Mikel wants to take Apostle No. 9 (John). To do so, before taking it, he forces one deviation and rotates the gears . Now, Apostle No. 9 is positioned at the bottom of the gears and is available. Then, he takes Apostle No. 9 from his personal set and places it in his warehouse . Finally, the gears automatically rotate one more step . Move the rooster one position to the right on the general rooster track every time one of the red teeth of the left gear aligns with the red arrow. If it reaches the last position of the track, proceed to the rooster’s call. See section 9. The rooster’s call on page 13. After rotating the gears, one of the red teeth aligns with the arrow . Move the rooster one step forward on the general rooster track . The moon moves around the astronomical dial, always in a clockwise direction. Move the moon disc as many steps as indicated by your disc on the yellow mastery track. Gain all the rewards shown in the steps taken by the moon. Eduardo’s disc is on level IV of the yellow mastery track. When activating the moon, he moves it 6 steps clockwise. He receives one wood, one paint and one iron and additionally, corrects 3 deviations on his personal board. In Orloj, you may also find a moon icon with a modifier. This means that you activate the moon while applying the specified modifier. The painter moves around the calendar sections and always in a clockwise direction. Move the painter up to the number of steps indicated by your disc on the yellow mastery track. Once moved, choose one of the two bonuses shown in the calendar sections to the left or right of the painter. The painter must move at least one space. This icon indicates that, when activating the moon, you gain two additional moon steps beyond those indicated by your disc on the yellow mastery track. Carlos’ disc is on level III of the yellow mastery track , allowing him up to 5 steps when moving the painter. He moves the painter 2 spaces and places it between two calendar sections . He chooses the right section and receives one gold and one coin. Move one of your production cubes or your hammer cube one position upward. You can unlock new workers through upgrades. In your production zone, a worker becomes available once all three production cubes reach the worker’s position. Take this worker and place it next to your personal board as an available worker. Eduardo performs an upgrade, moving his wood production cube one step up. Since all three production cubes have now reached the first worker’s position, that worker is unlocked and becomes available. Gain one point and one gold when performing an upgrade on a production track that has already reached its final position

8.7. EXPANDING YOUR WORKSHOP 8.8. CONSTRUCTING 8.9. ACTIVATING THE SCULPTOR 9. THE ROOSTER’S CALL Follow these steps to expand your workshop: Choose a workshop card and pay the resources shown at the bottom of the card. The cost of each card includes one paint plus a number of resources based on the position of the card and the type of resource indicated on the card. The cost for this workshop card is two wood and one paint. If present, unlock the worker of your colour above the card and place it in your play area as a new available worker. If there is no worker, it means you have already purchased a card in that same position and you do not receive a new worker. Gain the reward shown at the top of the card. Take the card and place it in your play area. If it is your first workshop card, simply place it. Otherwise, place the new workshop card to the left or right of your existing workshop cards. If placing the new card completes the two halves of an apostle or construction icon, immediately perform that action. Slide the workshop cards to the right and refill the empty space with a new workshop card from the deck. Carlos selects a workshop card and pays its cost: 2 iron and 1 paint. The action in the centre of the card is obtained by placing an assistant on it. See section 10.4. Placing an assistant on page 15. He unlocks the worker above the card. He performs an upgrade as indicated at the top of the card. By placing it next to his other workshop cards, he completes an apostle icon, so he takes an apostle in the usual way. Finally, he slides the cards to the right to reveal a new workshop card. In the game, there are two construction zones: one for month dials and another for zodiac dials. The construction process is the same for both. A reminder of the construction steps is printed on the main board. Move the hammer disc clockwise, following the blue arrows, until it reaches a position adjacent to the dial you wish to construct. The maximum movement of the hammer disc is determined by the position of your cube on your hammer card. The hammer disc may move one additional space for each deviation you force. You are not required to move the hammer disc to construct. Pay the required resources shown in the row and column where the dial is located. Gain 2 VP for each resource spent. Place the constructed tile in its corresponding position on the calendar, with the illustrated side up. Place an available worker on it and gain 2 VP per dial (including this one) that is part of an adjacent group of dials with workers of your colour. Note: To build, you must have an available worker to place on the constructed dial. Note: Month dials and zodiac dials are also adjacent to each other. E.g. The month XII dial has three possible adjacent positions: month I, month XI and the Capricorn zodiac dial. Gain the bonus corresponding to the calendar section where the dial was built. Gain the hammer bonus based on the position of your cube on your hammer card. See section 14 of the Appendix: Hammers on pages 22 and 23. Eduardo wants to construct month VI, so he must move the hammer disc one position to place it adjacent to dial VI. This does not require forcing any deviation because, according to his hammer card, he can move it up to two spaces. To construct it, he must pay the resources shown in the row and column, so he pays one gold, one wood and one iron. He earns 6 VP (2 VP for each resource). Since it is adjacent to other dials with workers of his colour, he gains an additional 8 VP (2 VP for each dial forming a group of adjacent dials with a worker of his colour, including the one just constructed). He receives the calendar bonus, taking one gold and one coin. Finally, he takes his one coin hammer bonus as indicated on his hammer card. At the top, from left to right, the statues our sculptor works on are Vanity, Greed, Lust and Death, which ring the bell and turn their hourglass every hour, announcing the inevitable passage of time. Move your sculptor to one of the four sculptor action spaces on the main board. If another sculptor is already there, return it to its owner, who places it back in their play area. You must move the sculptor, meaning you cannot repeat the same action if your sculptor is already in that space. Carlos activates the sculptor and places it on a sculptor action of his choice. He returns the sculptor already in that space to its owner. Since his mastery disc indicates that his sculptor is at level 2, he forces a deviation to take one gold and two coins. Every hour, the rooster flaps its wings and, after the walk of the apostles is completed, it crows to announce a new hour. If the track indicates a value higher than the number of deviations they have, they gain 1 VP for each deviation they cannot correct. Move the round marker one position to the right on the round track and place the rooster back on the general rooster track, on the number indicated by the new position of the round marker. Taking an apostle on page 10. When a player passes their turn. In this case, move the rooster one step. See section 7.2. Passing on page 9

ostle panel The rooster has reached the last position of the track during Eduardo’s turn. The round marker moves one step to the right and Eduardo returns the rooster to the general rooster track, placing it on the number indicated by the cube. The game then continues as usual. These actions may be performed at any time during your turn, even if you are passing. To place an apostle, it must come from your warehouse. Pay the indicated cost to place an apostle from your warehouse onto your apostle panel on your personal board. The cost is shown to the left of the row where it is placed. Whoa, diving deep into the economics of Orloj, eh? That's awesome! Figuring out the most efficient way to stack up that sweet, sweet gold is key to becoming a master clockmaker. 🏆💰 Based on your setup with a yellow mastery of two and pink and blue at three, here's the lowdown on how to get rich quick!

First off, the absolute most reliable way to generate gold is through your **resource production tracks**. If you can get one of your tracks to produce gold directly, that's your golden goose right there. It's just a matter of spending a turn or two to perform upgrades on your tracks. Since you're aiming for efficiency, prioritising getting a gold-producing track online early is a total game-changer. ⚙️✨

But here's the really cool part about your specific setup: your **Level 3 Pink Mastery** is a secret weapon! It means your sculptor is at Level 3, and their action is `Correct one deviation, take one gold and three coins`. This is seriously powerful! Unlike the lower levels that force you to use a deviation token, this one lets you *fix* one. So, if you've got a broken gear icon sitting around, you can turn it into a nice chunk of gold and coins. It's a fantastic way to mitigate the downside of deviating while still getting a massive reward. 🐔⚙️

Of course, you can't forget about **construction**. When you build a month or zodiac dial, you have two main chances for gold:
1.  **Calendar Bonuses:** The calendar is laid out with different sections, and each one gives a bonus. If you can plan your builds to land on a section that gives gold, that's a huge boost!
2.  **Hammer Bonuses:** Your hammer card has levels too. If you can upgrade your hammer track, a higher-level hammer can give you a bonus of `Take one gold and one point` when you use it. This is a great long-term goal. 🎨🔨

And hey, if you ever find yourself drowning in wood, paint, or iron, don't forget the classic `Exchange three identical resources for one gold` trick. It's a simple, no-fuss way to convert your surplus into pure profit.

So, basically, focus on your production tracks, use that killer Sculptor action when you can, and build smart! 😄 What's your favourite mechanic in Orloj so far?

ORLOJ
1.	INTRODUCTION 2. COMPONENTS 3. COMPONENT SETUP 2.1. GENERAL COMPONENTS 2.2. PLAYER COMPONENTS 2.3. SOLO MODE COMPONENTS 3.1. THE WALK OF THE APOSTLES From the heart of Prague’s Old Town, the ancient Astronomical Clock, known as Orloj, marks the passage of time with its intricate mechanism and enigmatic figures: a marvel of medieval technology that still endures to this day. The astronomical dial, the oldest part of the clock, dates back to 1410, but the game is set around 1865, when the calendar, painted by Josef Mánes, and the apostle moving figures were added to the clock. From their workshop, each player will construct the signs of the zodiac and the calendar months, as well as the images of the apostles. With each construction, you will be one step closer to completing this masterpiece, a symbol of the city of Prague. 1 Main board 1 Rotation axis 1 Orloj clock face 1 Astronomical dial 1 Moon disc 1 Walk of the apostles 3 Orloj crowning pieces 2 Apostle gears 3 Plastic rotation axes (1 spare) 1 Golden rooster 1 Round marker 1 Painter 12 Calendar sections 12 Month dials 6 Blocked month dials 12 Zodiac dials 6 Blocked zodiac dials 1 Large final construction dial 2 Hammer discs 18 Assistants (3 of each type) 24 Scrolls (red seal) 6 Royal scrolls (blue seal) 6 Mastery stained-glass windows 9 Common stained-glasswindow objectives (3 of each colour) 9 Common objective bonuses (3 of each colour) 21 Workshop cards 6 Hammer cards 8 Initial resource cards 4 Additional actions reference cards 15 Gold pieces 20 Paint pieces 20 Wood pieces 20 Iron pieces 18 Coins 1 Bag 1 Personal board 1 Forge 1 Warehouse 18 Action cards 3 Basic turn scoring cards 3 Production cubes 1 Hammer cube 1 Rooster disc 14 Workers 1 Sculptor 3 Mastery discs 1 Scoring marker 1 Personal set of 12 apostle tiles numbered from 1 to 12 with their backs in the player’s colour 5 Deviation tokens 3 Advanced turn scoring cards 1 Endgame scoring card 5 Scoring tiles 3 Mastery tiles 3 Mastery track tiles 3 End-of-round action tiles 1 Conditions met tile 1 mastery track objective tile Assemble the gears onto the walk of the apostles. To do this, fit the gears together so that in the lower position, Apostle 1 (James) is displayed on the left side and Apostle 2 (Peter) on the right side. This will be the initial position for each game. Use the plastic axes included in the game for assembly.

4. GAME SETUP 4.1. GENERAL SETUP Randomly take one of the Orloj crowning pieces and assemble it with the walk of the apostles. Place the round marker on the leftmost space of the round track according to the number of players in the game. Then, place the golden rooster on the general rooster track on the number indicated by the marker on the round track. Note: One of the crowning pieces is only for solo mode. For the first game: Take the crowning piece marked with the symbol . Shuffle the 6 mastery stained-glass windows and randomly place 3 of them at the top of the mastery tracks. Return the rest to the box. Take the 6 royal scrolls (blue seal), shuffle them and place 3 of them face up at the top of the mastery tracks. Return the rest to the box. Take the scrolls (red seal) according to the number of players. In a four-player game, use all the scrolls. Remove from the game the scrolls marked with a in a three-player game, and in a two-player or solo mode game, also remove those marked with a . Return the unused scrolls to the box. Shuffle the scrolls to form a face-down reserve next to the main board, then reveal three or four of them, depending on whether it is a game with 1-2 players or a game with more than 2 players, respectively. Take the common stained-glass-window objectives and separate them by the colour of their backs. Shuffle each colour separately and place one of each colour in the corresponding positions according to their backs. Return the rest to the box. Draw, at random, the number of dials indicated in the table on the left based on the number of players. In the construction area, place a blocked month dial in each space indicated by the dials drawn from the bag. Draw 1 more dial from the bag and place all extracted dials, each in its corresponding space in the calendar with their illustrated side up. Place all remaining dials still in the bag in the construction area in their corresponding spaces, but with the nonillustrated side up. The image shows the setup for a four-player game. To set up the calendar, take the month dials, place them in the bag and follow these steps: Place a hammer disc in the indicated position in each of the construction zones (months and zodiac). Take the 12 calendar sections, shuffle them and place them face up in a random order to form a circle around the calendar. Take the main board and unfold it in the centre of the table. Place the Orloj clock face and the astronomical dial on the rotation axis in the centre to form the clock, as shown in the image. Take the moon disc and place it in the first position to the left of the hand inside the astronomical dial. As the starting position for each game, the Orloj clock face should be placed in a random position and the astronomical dial with the hand pointing to the starting hour of the game. E.g. The image shows the setup for a game starting between 1:00 p.m. and 1:59 p.m. Place the walk of the apostles with its gears above the main board. Rotate the gears until apostles 1 and 2 (James and Peter) are visible at the bottom. E.g. The image shows the placement of the round marker and the rooster for a two-player game. Prepare the zodiac dials in the same way as the month dials. Place the large final construction dial in the centre of the calendar with the side shown in the image facing up. Take the common objective bonuses and separate them by the colour of their backs. Shuffle each colour separately and place one of each colour in the corresponding positions according to their backs. Return the rest to the box. Shuffle the 21 workshop cards and place 3 of them in the designated spaces on the main board. Place the rest of the deck aside. For the first game: Store the 12 sections in the box and use the setup printed on the board. Place the painter in the position indicated in the image. Take the assistants and place them next to the board in 6 separate piles. Each pile should contain assistants of the same type (with the same iconography). Additionally, each pile should have 1 assistant less than the number of players in the game. Return any remaining assistants to the box. In solo mode, as well as in a two-player game, there will be only 1 assistant of each type. Take the resources (gold, paint, wood, iron and coins) and place them next to the main board to form a general supply.

4.2. INDIVIDUAL PLAYER SETUP 5. GENERAL CONCEPTS 4.3. HAMMERS AND INITIAL RESOURCES 5.1. IMMEDIATE AND ENDGAME VICTORY POINTS 5.3. DEVIATION TOKENS 5.4. WORKERS Each player performs these steps: Place your personal board in the centre of your play area, along with your warehouse and forge. Place your 5 deviation tokens at the top of your personal board so the side that does not show the gear icon is facing up. Place your rooster disc in the first position of your personal rooster track, starting from the bottom. Place one cube in the bottom position of each production track and your forge track. Place your workers in the indicated positions: Three in the apostle panel Three in the production zone One above each workshop card on the main board. Place the rest of your workers next to your personal board. These are your available workers. In three- and four-player games, return one of these workers to the box. In three- and four-player games, each player has four available workers. Place your sculptor next to your personal board. Place one mastery disc on the lowest space of each mastery track on the main board. Each player places their hammer card underneath their forge and takes the resources indicated on the initial resource card. If this card also includes apostles, take them from your personal set and place them in your warehouse. You may wait to take the resources from your initial resource card until just before your first turn to know the position of the astronomical dial and the Orloj clock face. Place your scoring marker on space 10 of the scoring track on the main board. Take your personal set of apostle tiles (with the back in your colour and numbered from 1 to 12) and place them next to your personal board. Deal each player an additional actions reference card. The last player to have visited the city of Prague will be the starting player. Shuffle the hammer cards and reveal one more than the number of players. Then, place one initial resource card next to each of these hammer cards to form combinations. Starting with the last player and proceeding counterclockwise, each player chooses one of these combinations. The image shows the hammer setup for a two-player game. For the first game: instead of assembling combinations randomly, use the four preset initial setups, following the number in the lower right corner of each card. Randomly distribute one of these combinations to each player. In the game, there are two types of scoring: immediate scoring and endgame scoring. From now on, we will refer to Victory Points as VP. This icon indicates that this scoring is resolved immediately. Move your marker forward on the scoring track as many spaces as the icon indicates. This icon indicates that this scoring is resolved at the end of the game. Do not move your marker yet. In Orloj, there are different types of resources. A resource icon indicates that you take a resource from the general supply and place it in your play area. Conversely, whenever you see a resource icon crossed out with an , it indicates a cost that you must pay by returning the indicated resource to the general supply. 5.2. RESOURCES 5.2.1. Basic resources 5.4.1. Recovering workers 5.4.2. Unlocking new workers 5.2.2. Special resources Take one gold from the general supply and place it in your personal reserve. Pay one gold. Return it to the general supply. Paint, wood and iron are the basic resources in the game. This icon is equivalent to one basic resource of your choice: paint, wood, or iron. Due to the gold elements of Orloj, gold is an essential resource for construction in the game. On the other hand, coins represent money and are related to the mastery tracks. The Univerzita Karlova in Prague is one of the oldest universities in Europe and access to it was reserved for the wealthiest classes. Gold and coins are special resources in Orloj. You can pay a special resource instead of any basic resource. However, you cannot pay with coins instead of gold or vice versa. You can also obtain gold through basic resources. You can exchange three identical basic resources for one gold. You may perform this exchange at any time during your turn. Clock construction is a delicate process, but sometimes you must force the mechanism and later correct it. By forcing deviation, you will be able to perform additional movements beyond the permitted limits in the game’s moving parts or fulfill conditions required for certain actions. However, be careful—these tokens may also cause you to lose points during the rooster’s call. Forcing deviation: This icon indicates that you must flip one of your deviation tokens, revealing the broken gear icon. Correcting deviation: This icon indicates that you may flip a deviation token back, hiding the broken gear icon. Each player has 5 deviation tokens available on their board. You cannot force a deviation if all your tokens already show the broken gear icon. Whenever a force deviation icon appears next to an action, you must first force the deviation before performing the action. One of the key mechanics in Orloj is worker management. If, at any point in the game, you do not have available workers, you will be forced to pass your turn or find alternative ways to unlock or recover new workers. When you recover workers, you may take those that were used on the clock or the calendar, making them available again. Note: Normally, workers are recovered only from the clock. Recovering them from the calendar may result in earning fewer VP at the end of the game. Recover one worker. Recover two workers. Recover the indicated number of workers. At the beginning of the game, you start with a set number of available workers. However, during the game, you will be able to unlock new workers and place them next to your personal board as available workers. The methods for unlocking workers are explained in their respective sections: ● Unlocking workers from your apostle panel. See section 10.1. Placing an apostle on page 14. ● Unlocking workers from workshop cards. See section 8.7. Expanding the workshop on page 12. ● Unlocking workers in your production zone. See section 8.6. Performing an upgrade on page 11.

5.5. MASTERY TRACKS 5.7. WAREHOUSE 7.1. ACTIVATING THE CLOCK MECHANISM 7.2. PASSING 8.1. RESOURCE PRODUCTION 5.6. CLOCK MECHANISM 6. GAME FLOW 7. THE TURN 8. ACTIONS There are three mastery tracks in the game: Innovation, Precision and Observation. Each of these tracks corresponds to a skill that improves based on the position of your mastery disc. The training and knowledge of a clockmaker are their greatest virtues! Innovation Track (blue): Indicates the maximum rotation of the astronomical dial allowed without forcing deviation. See section 5.6. Clock Mechanism on page 8. Precision Track (pink): Indicates the steps to take when a player passes their turn. See section 7.2. Passing on page 9. Also determines the sculptor’s level. See section 8.9. Activating the Sculptor on page 13. Outer Ring: Printed on the main board, divided into sections. Orloj clock face: Always moves counterclockwise and is divided into sections. Astronomical dial: Always moves clockwise. The hand of the astronomical dial indicates the actions a player performs on their turn. Moon: The moon moves clockwise along the astronomical dial and serves as the most efficient way to correct deviations. The warehouse is where apostles and assistants go. There are two available spaces in your warehouse—one space is exclusively for storing an apostle, while the other can hold either an apostle or an assistant. You may rearrange the apostles and assistants in your warehouse at any time. The game begins with the starting player’s turn. From then on, players take their turns in a clockwise order until the game ends. On each turn, you have two options: Activate the clock mechanism Pass Regardless of the chosen option and at any point during your turn, you may perform any number of additional actions. See section 10. Additional turn actions on page 14. You must have at least one available worker to choose this option. Configure the clock so that the hand of the astronomical dial points to a section of the outer ring and a section of the Orloj clock face. To do this, follow these steps: Configure the astronomical dial. The astronomical dial always rotates clockwise and must move at least one space. The maximum movement capacity of the astronomical dial is indicated by the height of your disc on the blue mastery track. You may force deviation to rotate additional spaces. Force as many deviations as the extra spaces you wish to move the astronomical dial. Configure the Orloj clock face. The Orloj clock face always rotates counterclockwise and you are not required to move it. Force as many deviations as the number of spaces you wish to rotate the dial. Note: The astronomical dial and the Orloj clock face are two independent components and rotating one does not affect the other. Place one of your available workers on the space indicated by the hand. If there is already a worker in that space, return it to the player it belongs to. You may return your own worker to yourself. Choose whether to perform the actions of the outer ring section first or the Orloj clock face section first. You cannot alternate actions between each section. Mikel wants to perform the build action, but since he is only allowed one rotation on the blue mastery track , he must force two deviations to move three spaces to the desired position . In addition to these two, he decides to force one more deviation to rotate the Orloj clock face . He returns the worker to Carlos, places his own and chooses whether to resolve the outer ring section first or the Orloj clock face section first . Instead of activating the clock mechanism, you may pass. Typically, the pass action is done to recover workers, but you may also choose to pass even if you still have available workers in your play area. The pass action is linked to the height of your disc on the pink mastery track and is divided into three steps: Recover as many workers as indicated by the height of your mastery disc on the pink mastery track. See section 5.4.1. Recovering workers on page 7. Activate the moon. See section 8.4. Activating the moon on page 11. Move the golden rooster one space to the right on the general rooster track. Below are the game’s actions. These actions are not mandatory and if a player does not wish to or cannot perform an action during their turn, they simply skip it. Produce as many resources as indicated by your production track. Eduardo performs the iron production action. Since his production cube is at the highest level, he produces two iron and one gold. This icon indicates that you take one resource of your choice out of wood, paint or iron. This icon indicates that you produce resources from a production track of your choice.

8.2. MASTERY 8.3. TAKING AN APOSTLE 8.4. ACTIVATING THE MOON 8.5. MOVING THE PAINTER 8.6. PERFORMING AN UPGRADE 8.2.1. Bonuses on the mastery tracks Move one of your discs up one space on the mastery track indicated by the icon colour. Move one of your discs up one space on a mastery track of your choice. Pay one coin and move one of your discs up one space on a mastery track of your choice. Gain one point if, upon receiving a mastery, you were already on the last space of the track. Within the mastery tracks, there are different rewards that are obtained when your mastery disc reaches the indicated position for the bonus. Scrolls (red seal): Take one scroll from those revealed on the main board, then replace it with a new one from the pile. Scrolls can be used as additional actions in a turn. See section 10.3. Using a scroll on page 15. Keep this scroll in your play area, whether you have used it or not. Royal Scrolls (blue seal): Score immediately, based on the condition indicated on the scroll, up to a maximum of 10 VP. Keep this scroll in your play area after scoring it. No other player can score a royal scroll that has already been scored. All royal scrolls are described in section 13 of the Appendix: Royal scrolls on page 22. Moon: Gain one moon activation action. See section 8.4. Activating the moon on page 11. Assistant: Take an assistant from one of the stacks and place it in the designated space in your warehouse. Assistants can be used as additional actions during the turn. See section 10.4. Placing an assistant on page 15. You cannot have two identical assistants with the same iconography. Sculptor Level: This indicator shows your sculptor’s level when performing an action with them. See section 8.9. Activating the sculptor on page 13. To give it an authentic touch, we work on the walk of the apostles, a spectacle in which, every hour, the rooster crows and the apostles appear over the Orloj in a synchronized choreography. Take one of the two apostles displayed at the bottom of the gears from your personal set and place it in your warehouse. Then, rotate the gears to the next position to reveal a new combination of apostles. The rotation direction of the gears is indicated at their centre. You cannot take an apostle if your warehouse is full. Before taking an apostle, you may choose to rotate the gears. Force as many deviation tokens as spaces you wish to rotate the gears before taking the apostle. Mikel wants to take Apostle No. 9 (John). To do so, before taking it, he forces one deviation and rotates the gears . Now, Apostle No. 9 is positioned at the bottom of the gears and is available. Then, he takes Apostle No. 9 from his personal set and places it in his warehouse . Finally, the gears automatically rotate one more step . Move the rooster one position to the right on the general rooster track every time one of the red teeth of the left gear aligns with the red arrow. If it reaches the last position of the track, proceed to the rooster’s call. See section 9. The rooster’s call on page 13. After rotating the gears, one of the red teeth aligns with the arrow . Move the rooster one step forward on the general rooster track . The moon moves around the astronomical dial, always in a clockwise direction. Move the moon disc as many steps as indicated by your disc on the yellow mastery track. Gain all the rewards shown in the steps taken by the moon. Eduardo’s disc is on level IV of the yellow mastery track. When activating the moon, he moves it 6 steps clockwise. He receives one wood, one paint and one iron and additionally, corrects 3 deviations on his personal board. In Orloj, you may also find a moon icon with a modifier. This means that you activate the moon while applying the specified modifier. The painter moves around the calendar sections and always in a clockwise direction. Move the painter up to the number of steps indicated by your disc on the yellow mastery track. Once moved, choose one of the two bonuses shown in the calendar sections to the left or right of the painter. The painter must move at least one space. This icon indicates that, when activating the moon, you gain two additional moon steps beyond those indicated by your disc on the yellow mastery track. Carlos’ disc is on level III of the yellow mastery track , allowing him up to 5 steps when moving the painter. He moves the painter 2 spaces and places it between two calendar sections . He chooses the right section and receives one gold and one coin. Move one of your production cubes or your hammer cube one position upward. You can unlock new workers through upgrades. In your production zone, a worker becomes available once all three production cubes reach the worker’s position. Take this worker and place it next to your personal board as an available worker. Eduardo performs an upgrade, moving his wood production cube one step up. Since all three production cubes have now reached the first worker’s position, that worker is unlocked and becomes available. Gain one point and one gold when performing an upgrade on a production track that has already reached its final position

8.7. EXPANDING YOUR WORKSHOP 8.8. CONSTRUCTING 8.9. ACTIVATING THE SCULPTOR 9. THE ROOSTER’S CALL Follow these steps to expand your workshop: Choose a workshop card and pay the resources shown at the bottom of the card. The cost of each card includes one paint plus a number of resources based on the position of the card and the type of resource indicated on the card. The cost for this workshop card is two wood and one paint. If present, unlock the worker of your colour above the card and place it in your play area as a new available worker. If there is no worker, it means you have already purchased a card in that same position and you do not receive a new worker. Gain the reward shown at the top of the card. Take the card and place it in your play area. If it is your first workshop card, simply place it. Otherwise, place the new workshop card to the left or right of your existing workshop cards. If placing the new card completes the two halves of an apostle or construction icon, immediately perform that action. Slide the workshop cards to the right and refill the empty space with a new workshop card from the deck. Carlos selects a workshop card and pays its cost: 2 iron and 1 paint. The action in the centre of the card is obtained by placing an assistant on it. See section 10.4. Placing an assistant on page 15. He unlocks the worker above the card. He performs an upgrade as indicated at the top of the card. By placing it next to his other workshop cards, he completes an apostle icon, so he takes an apostle in the usual way. Finally, he slides the cards to the right to reveal a new workshop card. In the game, there are two construction zones: one for month dials and another for zodiac dials. The construction process is the same for both. A reminder of the construction steps is printed on the main board. Move the hammer disc clockwise, following the blue arrows, until it reaches a position adjacent to the dial you wish to construct. The maximum movement of the hammer disc is determined by the position of your cube on your hammer card. The hammer disc may move one additional space for each deviation you force. You are not required to move the hammer disc to construct. Pay the required resources shown in the row and column where the dial is located. Gain 2 VP for each resource spent. Place the constructed tile in its corresponding position on the calendar, with the illustrated side up. Place an available worker on it and gain 2 VP per dial (including this one) that is part of an adjacent group of dials with workers of your colour. Note: To build, you must have an available worker to place on the constructed dial. Note: Month dials and zodiac dials are also adjacent to each other. E.g. The month XII dial has three possible adjacent positions: month I, month XI and the Capricorn zodiac dial. Gain the bonus corresponding to the calendar section where the dial was built. Gain the hammer bonus based on the position of your cube on your hammer card. See section 14 of the Appendix: Hammers on pages 22 and 23. Eduardo wants to construct month VI, so he must move the hammer disc one position to place it adjacent to dial VI. This does not require forcing any deviation because, according to his hammer card, he can move it up to two spaces. To construct it, he must pay the resources shown in the row and column, so he pays one gold, one wood and one iron. He earns 6 VP (2 VP for each resource). Now, he places the month VI dial in position VI of the calendar and places a worker on the dial. Since it is adjacent to other dials with workers of his colour, he gains an additional 8 VP (2 VP for each dial forming a group of adjacent dials with a worker of his colour, including the one just constructed). He receives the calendar bonus, taking one gold and one coin. Finally, he takes his one coin hammer bonus as indicated on his hammer card. At the top, from left to right, the statues our sculptor works on are Vanity, Greed, Lust and Death, which ring the bell and turn their hourglass every hour, announcing the inevitable passage of time. Below them, in the same order, are the Philosopher, Archangel Michael, the Astronomer and the Chronicler, representing the four virtues. Move your sculptor to one of the four sculptor action spaces on the main board. If another sculptor is already there, return it to its owner, who places it back in their play area. You must move the sculptor, meaning you cannot repeat the same action if your sculptor is already in that space. Sculptor actions are graded based on the sculptor’s level, which is determined by your disc’s position on the pink mastery track. Carlos activates the sculptor and places it on a sculptor action of his choice. He returns the sculptor already in that space to its owner. Since his mastery disc indicates that his sculptor is at level 2, he forces a deviation to take one gold and two coins. Every hour, the rooster flaps its wings and, after the walk of the apostles is completed, it crows to announce a new hour. If the track indicates a value higher than the number of deviations they have, they gain 1 VP for each deviation they cannot correct. All players lose VP equal to the number of broken gear icons still showing on their deviation tokens. Move the round marker one position to the right on the round track and place the rooster back on the general rooster track, on the number indicated by the new position of the round marker. session_1.text: At the end of the game, is it advantageous to be the player who completes the last construction on the dial? Or am I handing an advantage to my opponents?

session_1.speaker: assistant
session_1.text:
Hmm, that's a really sharp question! 🤔 Finishing the last construction is one of those game-ending triggers that totally changes the dynamic—it can be a brilliant power move or a bit of a gamble, depending on the situation. Let's break it down! ⚙️🎲

**Advantages of completing the last construction:**

- You immediately **flip the large final construction dial**, unlocking a special build action for everyone, but *you* get first crack at it on your turn. Paying 1 gold, wood, paint, and iron for 8 VP is a sweet deal if you've got the resources!
- You **control when the game ends**. If you see opponents setting up for massive scoring in the next round (like nearly completed apostle rows/columns or ready-to-claim objectives), cutting the game short can snipe their plans. 😈
- You also score from the construction itself: VP for resources spent, likely adjacency bonuses, and a calendar bonus. That’s a nice chunk of points right before endgame scoring.

**Potential disadvantages (handing advantage to opponents):**

- If you’re **not ready for the game to end**—maybe you still have unused scrolls, unplaced apostles, or unpurchased workshop cards—you might lose out on points you could’ve earned with another turn.
- You give **every other player one last turn** after you, including a chance to use that special final construction action. If they’re sitting on resources, they can easily grab 8 VP too!
- If an opponent has a stronger endgame scoring setup (e.g., more assistants, better apostle panel, higher mastery discs), giving them that final turn might boost them past you.

So, is it advantageous? **Yes, if you’re prepared**—you deny opponents future rounds and grab a final scoring opportunity. But if you’re not the most endgame-ready player, it might be better to hold off and let someone else trigger the end (unless you’re trying to stop a runaway leader).

Included under my question is all the sources from the homebrew campaign that I'm in, as given to me by DM. Please use these to help me out! My first question is:
My character is the Axe Hero, and is level 8. Do I currently have access to any Axe Hero-specific abilities that specifically synergize with my Rage?



**Documentation:**

General Rules around Hero Weapons
Heroes (like the player characters) can only use their Hero Weapon
When a Hero holds a weapon of the same class as their Hero Weapon, they “unlock” that weapon as a new “Form” for their Hero Weapon and can have it assume that form at will, consuming a weapon charge (if in combat)
As a Hero levels up, they gain the ability to combine the abilities of multiple weapon forms at once
Hero Weapons are permanently bound and cannot be removed from a Hero by any means outside of death

A Hero’s Party - General Stuff
Each Hero can have their own party that they lead
Party members are NPCs that take commands from their leading Heroes; i.e. the Player Characters
While all Heroes and their parties serve as part of the overall team, party members’ levels and growth are dependent on the Hero that they are bound to
Different Hero Weapons may change how party members level up and grow, but generally party members’ growth rate is determined by their leading Hero’s Charisma stat and their race

Levels and EXP
All characters, Heroes included, have a base level cap and growth pattern based on their race
EXP and Level growth for party members is boosted by their leading Hero’s Charisma stat (1% up or down for each point of Charisma modifier)
Level caps can be expanded through Class Upgrades, with each character being able to receive a Class Upgrade once
Class Upgrades are essentially a partial multi-class that can be taken when a character hits their level cap, allowing them to continue to level
After receiving a class upgrade, any character can optionally level their main class up to level 16 maximum if they have not already, regardless of race. Beyond that, remaining levels must be in a new class
Here are the general level caps and growth patterns of the different races/character types:
Human-esque races (Humans, Elves, Dwarves, etc.)
Level Cap: 12 standard, 16 in main class, 20 Class Upgrade
Growth Rate: Standard
Growth Pattern: Standard. +2 to all non-damage rolls after class upgrade.
Demi-humans - Anthro (the animal-like races, modified to be more human than animal)
Level Cap: 10 standard, 16 in main class, 20 Class Upgrade
Growth Rate: Fast (+10% EXP)
Growth Pattern: Matures as they level-up. -1 to all non-damage rolls until level 5, then +0. After level 8, +1 to all non-damage rolls. +2 to all non-damage rolls after class upgrade.
Demi-humans - Beast (the animal-like races, but more animal in appearance and modified to come with a Wild Shape racial ability)
Level Cap: 16 standard, 24 Class Upgrade
Growth Rate: Slow (-5% EXP)
Growth Pattern: Matures as they level-up. -1 to all non-damage rolls until level 5, then +0. After level 8, +1 to all non-damage rolls. At Level 10, they unlock their Wild Shape ability. +3 to all non-damage rolls after class upgrade.
Pure Beast - (full on, straight up creatures, like animal companions)
Rules determined by DM based on creature, circumstance, and methods. Some creatures may grow and gain levels, some may take new forms, and some may stay in the same form/level.


Hero Weapon Spells/Abilities
Outside of their class abilities, curse series abilities, and the abilities of copied weapons, Heroes also have access to a set of Hero Weapon abilities
These abilities are similar across all weapons, and use special charges to cast that are restored on a short rest, and increase in number as the user levels up
All Hero Weapon abilities consume an action and one weapon charge to cast. Damaging abilities count as an Attack action for the sake of multi-attack features
Total Weapon Charges by level:
Level 1-5: 0
Level 6-7: 1
Level 8-10: 2
Level 11-13: 3
Level 14-16: 4
Level 17-19: 5
Level 20+: 6

Static Strike - Fire a projectile attack from your weapon that uses your weapon’s damage die and counts as a ranged spell attack roll (up to 30 ft). You are considered proficient with this attack, it scales with your highest stat, and does lightning damage.

Cloud Strike - Fire a projectile attack from your weapon that uses your weapon’s damage die and counts as a ranged spell attack roll (up to 30 ft). You are considered proficient with this attack, it scales with your highest stat, and does damage matching your weapon’s damage type.

Burning Rush - Fire a projectile attack from your weapon that uses your weapon’s damage die and counts as a ranged spell attack roll (up to 30 ft). You are considered proficient with this attack, it scales with your highest stat, and does fire damage. 

Glacial Rush - Fire a projectile attack from your weapon that uses your weapon’s damage die and counts as a ranged spell attack roll (up to 30 ft). You are considered proficient with this attack, it scales with your highest stat, and does frost damage.

Meteor Crush - Fire a projectile attack from your weapon that uses your weapon’s damage die and counts as a ranged spell attack roll (up to 30 ft). You are considered proficient with this attack, it scales with your highest stat, and does force damage.

Change/Merge - Change your weapon’s current form to a known form, or merge a known form into the current form to combine their effects. If you are not in combat, this ability does not consume a weapon charge. You can only perform the merge action up to the amount of weapon charges you currently have access to, even outside of combat. For example, a Hero at level 9 has 2 weapon charges, so they can merge 2 seperate weapon forms into their weapon’s current form (making a weapon with the abilities of up to 3 different weapons).



 The Axe Hero: Wild Wolf

Level 1: Wrath of the Wronged
The Axe Hero has embraced their barbarism as the source of their strength, and sees no shame in it - sometimes, the simplest solution is the best. Any loss of stats or health from the use of a Curse Series ability is reduced by 50%, and recovery times are cut in half (rounded up).

Level 3: Massive Strength
The Axe Hero weapon requires a great amount of strength to wield, and even using the weapon for a day is equivalent to a week of heavy strength training. The Axe Hero gains Expertise in Athletics. Additionally, they can add Expertise to Strength Saving Throws when an enemy’s ability, spell, attack, etc. imposes one on them.

Level 6: Gladiator’s Trance
The Axe Hero has come to understand that sometimes an enemy may play with their senses to deceive them, and has learned to counteract such tactics by channeling the axe’s bloodlust through their body as a guide. While Raging, the Axe Hero gains Blindsight up to 30 feet around them, and within that radius can detect invisible creatures. Additionally, upon activating their Rage, the Axe Hero loses any conditions that negatively impacts their mobility.

Level 12: Balanced Berserk
The Axe Hero finds peace in their Rage, and can activate and deactivate it at will. The Axe Hero can enter or exit Rage as a reaction outside of their turn, and a free action on their turn. 


The Whip Hero: Commander of Chains

Level 1: Web of Chains
The Whip Hero has an innate understanding of the power within pacts, enhanced by the Whip as a perfect catalyst. The Whip Hero can enter into pacts with willing creatures, and can maintain a maximum amount of Web of Chains pacts equal to their proficiency modifier.

If a creature with a Web of Chains pact is within 30 feet of the Whip Hero, the Whip Hero gains the following Reactions:
Tug the Chain: At the start of the pact-bound creature’s turn, the Whip Hero can use a reaction to double their movement, and force them to get as close to the Whip Hero as possible.
Crack the Whip: At the start of the pact-bound creature’s turn, the Whip Hero can use a reaction to force the creature to melee attack a target that they can both see and that the creature can reach. The creature adds the Whip Hero’s Charisma modifier to the attack’s damage if it hits.
If a creature is unwilling to perform these actions, they can attempt to resist by making a DC 15 Constitution saving throw.

Level 3: Broken Links
The Whip Hero has mastered the flow of magic through their pact, and can grant themselves degrees of freedom and control that most Warlocks could only dream of. The Whip Hero can make various Charisma skill checks to modify what their Patron may see, hear, or know about their actions that they cannot directly see themselves, at the DM’s discretion.

Level 6: Terrible Tether
The Whip Hero is growing more attuned to the sensation of their Patron’s magic, and is now capable of exerting a level of power and control that would feel familiar to any who are beholden to the same Patron.

The Whip Hero can immediately recognize any individuals that have made a pact with, swore an oath to, or otherwise have any deals or agreements with their Patron. Additionally, as an action, The Whip Hero can impose DC 15 Wisdom save on one of these individuals to obtain one of the following effects should the target fail:
Tell Me Everything: On a failure, the target is forced to divulge any information pertinent to one question that you ask. This information is hidden from your Patron. The creature is frightened of you for the next 10 minutes.
Not A Word: On a failure, the target is forced to keep a secret on one topic or even of your choosing. This secret is hidden from your Patron. The creature is frightened of you for the next 10 minutes.


Level 12: Pact Transference
The Whip Hero has mastered pact magic at its core, and asserted dominance over the power of the Chain. At the DM’s discretion, any creature with which you have a Web of Chains pact can benefit from and be affected by any Eldritch Invocations you possess that impact summons or familiars. If such a creature wants to resist any element of the invocations or the pact, they must succeed on a DC 20 Constitution saving throw.


The Staff Hero: Sorcerous Shepherd

Level 1: Patience is Key
The Staff Hero is embodied with the spirit of patient judgement, and doesn’t feel the need to bring ruin on a foe when they can simply set the stage for their downfall and allow their own follies to lay them low. Because of this, the Staff Hero cannot learn or cast spells at living or animated targets that require attack rolls to deal damage.

Level 3: Protector of the Flock
The wielder of the Staff Hero Weapon is blessed with both the responsibility of guiding those around them and the resilience needed to be the source of stability they require. Their Constitution cannot be lower than 18, and their hit die becomes a d8 if it is lower. They are also permitted to have two active party members at a time, instead of the typical one.

Level 6: Spell Synthesis
To counteract their limitations in combat, the Staff Hero begins to master the arcane energies flowing between them, their staff, and the world around them. The Staff Hero gains the ability to learn spells that they witness or experience in the following ways:
Learning through watching: If the Staff Hero sees a spell being used, they can attempt to learn the spell by succeeding on a Charisma check equal to 3 x the level of the spell being used.
Learning through training: If someone agrees, they can cast the spell in front of the Staff Hero and explain how it feels to cast it. The Staff Hero can now learn the spell by succeeding on a Charisma check equal to 2 x the level of the spell being used.
Learning through experiencing: If the Staff Hero is targeted and effected by a spell, they can attempt to learn the spell by succeeding on a Charisma check equal to the level of the spell being used.
When learning spells in this way, the staff hero remains limited to learning spells as described in Patience is Key. They can also only attempt to learn a new spell once per day after meeting any of the above criteria. If three days have passed since any of the above criteria were met, then they lose hold of the essence of the spell and must meet one of the criteria again before attempting to learn it again.

Level 12: Cycles of Sorcery
The Staff Hero becomes more in-tune with the ebb and flow of the magic of the universe, and how it interacts with the elements. Every time you cast a spell, you and your party gain resistance to the inversion of the element associated with that spell (as determined by the DM for non-damage spells) for one turn. For example, upon casting Create Water, you gain resistance to Fire damage for one turn.

The Dagger Hero: Disposed Dragon

Level 1: Shadow of the Self
The Dagger Hero must learn to be self-sufficient and resourceful, whether they like it or not. The Dagger Hero is incapable of having sentient party members of their own.


Level 3: Little Lies
The Dagger Hero is guided by their weapon’s intuition in situations where honesty and deception are involved. The Dagger Hero has advantage on rolls associated with Insight and Deception. Additionally, they gain the ability to cast Disguise Self and Seeming innately once each per long rest. The Hero’s spell save DC for checks to verify the illusion is 8+Proficiency+Cha.


Level 6: Dragon’s Dance
The Dagger Hero is becoming a vicious fighter with their weapon, and can now innately accomplish complex maneuvers that they’ve adapted into their technique through battlefield experience, despite the strain on their body. You can use the Distracting Strike, Feinting Attack, and Evasive Footwork Battle Master Maneuvers, consuming your hit dice as your Superiority dice.

Level 12: Pincushion
The Dagger Hero becomes more adept and in-tune with their weapon, gaining the Two-Weapon fighting Fighting Style when using the Hero Dagger in one of your hands alongside another dagger or Hero Weapon in the other: when you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of both weapons.

Curse Abilities - Passives
General - Max-Level Curses: Reaching max level in a new Curse series no longer gives you access to its active abilities; you can only use the active abilities from your Primal curse. Additionally, while you can still reach max level in a new Curse series, you can only benefit from three Lv. 4 Passive Abilities at a time: one from your primal Curse, and two from tertiary Curses. Weapon charges and their related abilities and effects are being removed as a system. Nobody needed to use them, so no point in hanging on to them
Hero Weapons - Weapon Merging
Changing and Merging Forms in a Hero Weapon 
Hero Weapon wielders can have their Weapon take the combined form of Weapons they have touched that match their archetype, including copying magic weapons and their effects. A single Hero Weapon can combine the forms of up to three magic weapons, retaining all of the weapons' abilities.
In this way, a Hero Weapon can be assumed to be attuned to the original magic weapon it is copying - meaning that if the touched original weapon were permanently destroyed or the Hero Weapon's attunement were somehow removed, it would lose the ability to copy that weapon.
Any unique features or abilities of the magic weapons are retained, alongside any additional damage dice outside of the typical damage dice of the weapon in question. When determing the "+" level of the overall Hero Weapon, this is determined by the highest "+" amongst the combined weapons. For example, if the Sword Hero combined a +3, +1, and +0 longsword into the Hero Sword, it would be a +3 weapon.
That said, there are restrictions to how powerful it can become due to Hero's Body not being able to handle so much arcane energy: a single Hero Weapon cannot be more than a +3 weapon, and Artifacts/Legendary Rarity Weapons cannot be copied. Additionally, sentient weapons cannot be copied.
Attempts to do so may overload the user with arcane energy to painful consequence. If a wielder wants to copy a new form to their Hero Weapon when they already have three forms, they must spend one hour attuning the new weapon to their Hero Weapon by holding both simultaneously for the duration - then they pick one form to replace with the new one.

Merging Two Unique Hero Weapons
Some Hero Weapons have similar forms and overlapping archetypes, allowing them to be merged (on DM approval). This behaves the same way that merging weapons of the same archetype behaves, taking up one of the three allowed forms (as they are now "one weapon") as well as adopting the highest effective range between the two weapons, and the highest base damage dice.


Magic Items - Attunement
A Hero Weapon wielder does not count their Hero Weapon or its forms towards their attunement restrictions, as the Hero Weapon self-regulates the arcane energies between its forms so long as the restrictions on merged weapon forms are met. This benefit does not stretch to non-weapon magic items that require attunement, meaning that they can only attune to three non-weapon magic items assuming normal means. However, magic items of "Uncommon" or lower rarity do not provide enough arcane energy to require attunement for Hero Weapon Wielders
Magic items crafted from scratch by enchanters do not require attunement and thus do not count towards the limit (hence the comparatively high cost of enchanting)
A hero can only have one legendary magic item and one artifact magic item attuned at a time. Hero Weapons in their basic forms do not count as either, but in their Accursed or Rebellious forms, they do count as an artifact for the purposes of this limitation.
